featured_reviews.name: Amit Khopade
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let’s be honest, 90% of the places that go viral on Instagram turn out to be a total trap. But this one? It is the rare, absolute 10/10 exception.
It is a brisk walk from the JB Nagar metro station, and you can't miss it because the storefront glows so beautifully in the evening. I ordered the Kaaram Dosa (their spicy garlic dosa), and it was genuinely marvelous. That fiery garlic punch was so spot on that I was literally licking my fingers by the end. Plus, the order came out super fast and the quality was top-notch.
Unlike most cramped, overhyped cafes, the interiors here are gorgeous and there is actually plenty of space to sit and breathe. I am already planning to make this a regular spot just so I can conquer their entire menu. Totally worth the walk and the hype, aankh band karke just go for it.

featured_reviews.name: Beauty By Benifer
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re searching for a perfect South Indian meal in Mumbai without breaking the bank, then you need to stop at Cafe Idlay in JB Nagar. It is a charming, quaint little spot with lovely alfresco seating. The service over here is quick. However the food is the real star here.
We tried a bunch of dishes and honestly, their Thatte Idlis might be some of the best I’ve ever had. We also tried their Medhu Vadas, Open Benne Dosa, and the Rawa Masala Dosa all were delicious. Do try their Goti Bhajis and the Sheera if you have a sweet tooth. We also tried their filter coffee which was great.

featured_reviews.name: Alston Alvares
featured_reviews.review_text:
WORST SERVICE EVER!

I had called up the so called cafe @ 9:25 asking for a reservation! I was told the place is empty, so come.

Literally 5 minutes later @ 9:30 we arrived to the place completely packed.

I told the guy serving tables,”I called only 5 minutes ago” His response was “Sir har minute table barta hai” very rudely.

We chose to wait since we have been wanting to eat here since a very long time.

We waited for more than 30 minutes in the indoor part of the restaurant next to the service area. I didn’t see a single table getting empty every minute as the guy said.

There was a table for 2 about to get empty, so we stood next to them so that we can sit there.

We table got empty. We sat there. I kept my belongings on the chair and went inside to the service area to place the order.

I came back near the table and the guy was rudely telling us to get up. There were 2 people that waited only 5 minutes but had placed orders. So he made us get up and went acting like he’s doing something. He started ignoring us.

We had to immediately leave the place. He was being rude since the beginning.

Extremely disappointed by this establishment! People don’t deserve to be treated so rudely by such unprofessional employees.

This is by far my worst experience after wanting to visit this place for months.

I would really suggest everyone to just go to Amar Juice Centre! It only a few meters away. They have never treated their customers so badly.

It’s a shocker to not be able to eat at Idlay after waiting for 30+ minutes! It’s just saddening to have such an experience.

Completely ruined the mood.

No Cafe/Restaurant can work if their management is this bad.

WORST SERVICE!

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Mutuswami Cafe in Khar and really enjoyed the overall experience. The place has a simple, casual vibe but serves a wide variety of dishes—from authentic South Indian options to Mumbai street-style favourites.

The benne dosa stood out with its crispy texture and buttery flavour, while the idli was soft and fresh. The cheese pav bhaji and mushroom sukha combo added a nice desi touch to the meal. The mango milkshake and mango sheera were rich, sweet, and perfect to end on a high note.

Service was quick, though it can get a bit crowded during peak hours. Overall, it’s a great place for breakfast or a casual meal with good food and decent pricing. Would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: sourabh debnath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at muttuswami Khar🌟
Started with the refreshing Kala Khatta and Aam Panna coolers — both were perfect for the Mumbai heat. The Ghee Podi Idli was super soft and flavourful, while the Masala Benne Dosa was buttery, crisp and delicious. For mains, the Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam and Chettinad Biryani were packed with authentic flavours and tasted amazing. Ended the meal with Payasam and Vanilla Gelato which made for the perfect dessert combo. Great food, comforting flavours and an overall amazing dining experience. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Mahima Pal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Khar outlet recently and absolutely loved the whole experience 🫶🏻

The café has such a warm and cozy vibe with a perfect blend of authentic South Indian flavours and modern café aesthetics. Every dish felt comforting, flavourful, and beautifully prepared.

We started with the Cheese Onion Uttappa which was soft, perfectly cooked, and loaded with cheese without overpowering the authentic taste. The Mutuswami Special Benne Dosa with paneer was honestly one of the highlights 🤤 crispy on the outside, buttery, rich, and filled generously with flavourful paneer stuffing.

The Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam was another standout dish. The appams were soft and fluffy while the mushroom preparation had a beautiful spicy South Indian flavour that paired so well together. We also tried the Paneer Cheese Grilled Sandwich which was super cheesy, crisp, and comforting.

For drinks, the Chikoo Milkshake was thick, creamy, and refreshing, while the Kala Khatta Cooler from their summer specials was tangy, nostalgic, and perfect for the Mumbai heat.
Ended the meal with Mango Sheera and it was the sweetest ending possible 🤌🏻 warm, rich, and full of mango flavour without being overly sweet.

Loved the quality, presentation, ambience, and overall experience. Definitely a place I’d love visiting again for comforting South Indian food with a modern twist.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami is one of those simple, comforting south indian food places which serve superb food. Calm and relaxed vibe - no rush, no noise just pure happiness. We absolutely loved the Paper masala Dosa, and podi idli.. two of my favs here. Apart from that they also serve Grilled Sandwiches, Pav Bhaji and an amazing line up of dosas and juices.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Muttuswami Café with my skeptical, firang partner. He loved it, and so did I.

We had the Muttuswamy Special Benne Dosa, which is a mix of Benne Dosa, Masala Dosa and Ghee Podi Dosa. We also had Idli Vada Rasam, Plain and Hazelnut Filter Coffee, and a Pineapple Sheera to top it off. All of it was delicious, as well as pleasing to the eye!

The restaurant has been done up beautifully - it feels like you're walking into another world. It's super clean, and all the little touches - from the dabbara set for the filter coffee, to the paan box for the mukhwaas - serve to further elevate the experience.

Special thanks to Gaurav for being so patient and helpful.

I only dock one star because the AC wasn't working, and it's upwards of 35 degrees C right now. But honestly, the food was worth it.

10/10, would recommend!

We recently visited Bawri for lunch, and the experience was truly amazing. The restaurant has beautiful, aesthetic interiors with a warm and elegant vibe that makes it perfect for a relaxed dining experience.

We started with Mutton Kakori Kebab and Chicken Smoked Tikka, both perfectly cooked and packed with rich flavors. Alongside, the Hibiscus Cranberry Lemonade and Kaji Lemon Ice Tea were refreshing and well-balanced.

For mains, the Bawri Butter Chicken with Bawri Naan was creamy and indulgent, while the Mutton Biryani stood out with its aromatic spices and tender meat.

featured_reviews.name: falguni doshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bawri was our family lunch place last week and it was a pleasant experience, the interiors are good and the staff took good care of us. These dishes are what we liked the most - you can definitely try them.

Dhakai Chaat, Ghugni and Gutti Aloo - we wanted to try something unique and they suggested this lesser known chaat from East India. The Gutti Aloo in the center was really tasty while the ghugni was creamy and comforting.

Dal Makhani with Bawri Naan - A must try from my side, the dal makhani was really top notch! The flavours were unlocked via slow cooking and it was really rich. The Bawri naan as suggested by the staff paired really well and gave it a nice garlicky spicy touch. Very good pairing and 100% recommend

Bawri Jamun - We ended with this dessert as we love gulab jamun and this was just superb! I especially loved the crunchy white chocolate at the bottom and this is really heavy - so leave some space for it. My husband and daughter loved the rabdi and we packed some more for them.

Very good place for family plans, if you like Indian food - you can definitely visit 💯

featured_reviews.name: Kaira Goradia

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh

Vihara The International by Tunga is one of the best pure vegetarian restaurants in Mumbai and we had an excellent experience during our visit. The place offers a warm, lively atmosphere and serves high quality vegetarian food that feels both comforting and flavour packed. We were especially happy to see how consistent the service and food quality were even on a busy day.

We ordered the Veg Cheese Seekh Kabab, Paneer Crispy, Veg Pot Rice and Veg Kheema Masala and each dish tasted fresh and well prepared. The refreshing Pink Melon Juice and Strawberry Black Grape mocktail added a nice touch to the meal, followed by the delicious Chickoo Halwa that completed our dining experience perfectly. Everything felt thoughtfully made which makes this restaurant a great pick for family dinners and weekend outings.

If you are searching for the best vegetarian food in Andheri East or looking for top rated pure veg restaurants near Mumbai airport, Vihara The International by Tunga is definitely worth visiting. The flavours, cleanliness, service and overall value make it one of the most reliable vegetarian dining spots in the area. We highly recommend this restaurant for anyone who enjoys hearty vegetarian meals and memorable dining experiences.

The staff is courteous and helpful, adding to the pleasant experience. The menu is extensive, featuring Chinese, South Indian, Italian, and North Indian cuisines.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Vihara by Tunga and had a truly satisfying meal! Tried a variety of south indian dishes that this place is famous for and each one stood out in its own way:

•Medu Wada– Crispy on the outside, soft and airy inside, served hot with chutney and sambar. The texture and flavour were just right.

•Rawa Masala Dosa – Light, crisp and beautifully roasted. It had a lovely crunch, and the potato masala was flavourful without being too oily.

•Gini Dosa their speciality was the highlight! Perfectly spicy, well-seasoned and packed with flavour. The unique spread of chutney and masala inside really makes it stand out.

•Royal Falooda– A rich and refreshing treat to end the meal. Layered well, not overly sweet, and very indulgent.

•Filter Coffee– Authentic South Indian filter coffee with the perfect balance of strength and froth. A must-try if you enjoy strong coffee.

•Chiku Halwa– A pleasant surprise! Smooth, warm, and packed with the natural sweetness of chikoo, with a melt-in-the-mouth texture.

Service was quick and pleasing, and the lively ambience adds to the dining experience. The place attracts a big office-going crowd, especially during peak hours, so it’s best to plan your visit accordingly. Overall, a great spot for delicious and comforting South Indian food!
